meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 14:30 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Ross (CTO), Priya Nair (ML Eng), Sam Ortiz (PM)
summary: Intro discovery focused on Redwood PLG quickstart path: free credits, time-to-first-token, SDK experience, and evaluation criteria for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is evaluating latency/cost tradeoffs and needs security docs for enterprise review.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thank you for making time. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the ae on this account, and with me is liam our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Evan Ross: good, thanks maya. excited to learn a bit about the quickstart. we got your signup invite last week.
[00:11] Priya Nair: hey, yes thanks. i'm priya on the ml side. main goal is to get something up end-to-end quickly and then run latency/cost checks.
[00:17] Sam Ortiz: and i'm sam, product. i'll be coordinating use-cases and stakeholders.
[00:22] Liam Patel: great. quick agenda: talk quickstart flow, free credits & time to first token, what success looks like for you, and then security questions. sound good?
[00:28] Evan Ross: yep that's perfect.
[02:05] Maya Chen: so just to kick off — are you prototyping inside any cloud or on-prem infra today? what's your stack look like?

[02:12] Priya Nair: we're in aws primarily, couple k8s clusters. currently using a hosted api from another vendor for internal experiments, but costs spiked when we started load-testing. latency is okay for batch but for interactive features we need sub-200ms tail ideally.
[02:30] Liam Patel: ok got it. when you say tail, is that p95, p99?

[02:33] Priya Nair: p95 around 150-200ms would be acceptable; p99 is less critical but we'd like to know the behavior. our throughput will start small — maybe 10 qps average, bursty peaks to 100 qps during events.
[02:45] Sam Ortiz: timeline wise we're trying to have a demo to execs in six weeks. so quick iteration and predictable costs are key.

[03:01] Maya Chen: perfect. the PLG quickstart path is designed for this — self-serve sign up, immediate free credits, and a few SDK examples to get you to first-token within minutes. liam do you want to talk about the dev flow?

[03:12] Liam Patel: sure. when you sign up you get free credits that map to hosted api usage. we provide CLI + python/js SDKs, plus a simple curl example. typical time-to-first-token for a developer in our tests is under 10 minutes — often less — you can paste an api-key into env and call a generate endpoint. we've also got a short notebook that walks through embeddings and chat flows.
[03:31] Priya Nair: nice. one question — do the free credits allow for dedicated benchmarking or are they restricted to hosted only?

[03:36] Maya Chen: the free credits are for hosted usage. if you want dedicated reserved capacity benchmarks we can spin up a short dedicated eval but that usually is sales-assisted and may need a small contract depending on scale. however for initial latency / correctness checks hosted often suffices, and we can provide guidance on config to emulate dedicated settings.
[04:02] Evan Ross: and on the hosted side, what's the mixing rules — can we pin model versions or is it rolling?

[04:07] Liam Patel: you can pin specific model versions at the request-level or create routes pinned to a model. Redwood also supports automatic fallback to cheaper/compatible variants if you configure routing policies, but for evals you can lock it down.
[04:22] Sam Ortiz: curious about cost modeling — we're highly sensitive. do you have per-token estimates or tooling to predict costs based on our expected prompts?

[04:30] Maya Chen: yes, the console gives token-level cost breakdowns. we also have a 'Optimize' guide that suggests batching, caching and quantization profiles. for quickstart we can show a simple cost projection sheet if you share a sample prompt set.
[05:05] Priya Nair: we can share a small sample. also security — we have to present SOC2 to legal, plus SSO + SAML requirements and ability to use our KMS for keys if we go private.

[05:15] Liam Patel: absolutely. Redwood Hosted is SOC2 compliant; for Private deployments we offer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering or on-prem packages. we also log request-level audit trails and have RBAC.
[05:29] Evan Ross: when you say private on-prem package, what's the typical lift? we're not ruling it out but want to understand timing — especially if we need it for sensitive PII workloads.

[05:37] Maya Chen: typical private deployments are enterprise conversations — usually a few weeks to provision and integrate depending on network. Dedicated in a VPC is faster and often hits the sweet spot: customer data stays within their network and we provide a private control plane option.

[06:05] Priya Nair: ok good. for benchmarking, we want to test both latency and throughput using a 4k context model for summarization and a cheaper 1k model for completions. do you support longer contexts?

[06:15] Liam Patel: yes, runtime supports modern attention optimizations and we've got quantized variants. longer context behavior depends on model architecture; we can recommend kernels and config. for 4k you'll see different costs and throughput than 1k, we'll share suggested batch sizes and kv-cache settings.
[07:02] Sam Ortiz: are there any gotchas with the SDKs? sometimes other vendors have different tokenization behavior from the model library we use.

[07:09] Liam Patel: tokenization should match the model. our SDK exposes tokenizers and a small helper to calculate tokens client-side. occasionally the auto-transcription of model names in our docs got garbled — sorry about that — but under the hood it's consistent.
[07:35] Evan Ross: good to know. also curious about rate limits and quotas; we'd like to protect production endpoints but allow spikes during demos.
[07:44] Maya Chen: you can configure per-route quotas and burst capacity. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and burst options. we can configure autoscaling policies too.
[08:05] Priya Nair: for the demo we might want to simulate 100 qps bursts; would hosted be able to handle that?

[08:12] Liam Patel: hosted can handle that but behavior depends on model and concurrency. for guaranteed tail-latency you'd typically go Dedicated. for evaluation, hosted plus our guidance will let you simulate the burst and we can monitor throttling behavior.
[09:01] Sam Ortiz: procurement question — any standard msa or do you require custom terms for dedicated/private?

[09:07] Maya Chen: we have a standard MSA and an enterprise addendum for private/dedicated deployments. i'll share the legal pack. smaller PLG contracts can be fully self-serve up to a certain usage threshold.

[09:25] Evan Ross: perfect. i'm going to be honest — our engineering lead cares a lot about ops: KV cache management, serving runtime, and autoscaling. can liam give a quick sketch of the runtime features?

[09:33] Liam Patel: sure. the serving runtime focuses on continuous batching, efficient kv-cache handling, and quantization-friendly paths. it chooses kernels based on sequence-length distribution and hardware. we also do smart routing by policy so you can route for latency or cost. in practise that means fewer cold starts and better, more predictable tail latencies.
[10:12] Priya Nair: that sounds promising. any published benchmarks or do you have a sample spreadsheet?
[10:16] Liam Patel: we keep benchmark sheets we can share; i'll attach one with typical p95/p99 numbers across common models and hardware. note results vary by workload but it provides a baseline.
[11:00] Maya Chen: quick question — what's your evaluation criteria? what does success look like for you in the six-week demo?

[11:08] Sam Ortiz: success is 1) a working demo for execs, 2) measured p95 under 200ms for interactive flows, and 3) a cost projection that is clearly better than our current hosted vendor when scaled.
[11:22] Priya Nair: and from an ml perspective, we want reproducible outputs for our prompt set and the ability to run A/B between model variants easily.

[11:30] Maya Chen: great — that's actionable. we'll focus quickstart on getting you to first-token and then run a small benchmark on your sample prompts. i'll include the free credits and an example notebook.
[12:10] Evan Ross: on the free credits — any restrictions on rate or models?

[12:14] Maya Chen: credits are usable across hosted models; they're metered like normal usage. there are soft rate limits for new accounts but we can temporarily raise them for evaluation if you ask and we coordinate with the se team.
[12:34] Priya Nair: good. also SSO — we use okta. can we get SAML on the team portal so we can manage access?
[12:40] Liam Patel: yes, SAML/SSO via Okta is supported. for private deployments we can integrate with your IdP for RBAC and also support SCIM for provisioning.
[13:05] Sam Ortiz: one thing — our legal will almost certainly ask about data retention and audit logs. do you retain requests on hosted?

[13:13] Maya Chen: by default hosted retains request logs for a limited window for observability; we offer data retention controls and an option for no retention if you move to Private. i'll include details in the security pack.
[13:28] Evan Ross: thanks. anything else we should share to help you scope the demo?
[13:33] Priya Nair: i'll share a sample of about 50 prompts representing completions and longer summarization tasks, plus a traffic profile for qps and burstiness.
[13:40] Maya Chen: perfect. that will help liam craft the benchmark. we'll also request an example curl + sdk snippet so your devs can run it locally.

[14:05] Liam Patel: i can also prepare a short checklist for running a time-to-first-token test: signup, install sdk, env var, run example, measure latency. that usually gets a dev to token in under 10 minutes.
[14:25] Sam Ortiz: great — dev velocity is important.
[15:05] Priya Nair: another quick question on private networking: do you support VPC peering or private link?
[15:11] Liam Patel: we support VPC peering and private connectivity options depending on the cloud. for on-prem we have an appliance option. specifics depend on your networking and security policies.
[15:30] Evan Ross: ok. so next steps — share the quickstart and credits, share security docs, schedule se-led demo and we'll send sample prompts. does that match everyone's understanding?

[15:40] Maya Chen: yes. i'll send the quickstart guide today and include the credits link. liam will follow up with the benchmark sheet and checklist. we'll propose two times for a 45 minute dive next week.
[15:56] Priya Nair: sounds good. one more: is there a sandbox org where we can invite our devs so they don't touch production?
[16:02] Maya Chen: yes, we can create a sandbox org under your account with limited scopes — i'll include instructions.
[16:25] Evan Ross: wonderful. any potential objections internally we should be aware of? costs and vendor lock-in are usual suspects.

[16:33] Maya Chen: totally. we emphasize the unified api so migration is straightforward and we provide exportables for model configs. on costs, the optimize toolkit can show batching and quantization wins to reduce per-token costs.
[17:02] Sam Ortiz: ok that's helpful.

[20:00] Liam Patel: just to call out a technical note — if you want to emulate dedicated behaviour on hosted during tests, use a pinned model route and request-level headers for batch sizing; i'll document the exact headers.
[20:24] Priya Nair: perfect. also curious about observability — do you surface per-route p95/p99 and token-level breakdowns?
[20:31] Liam Patel: yes, console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost, tracing hooks, and error analysis. we can also ship logs to your SIEM if needed.
[22:15] Evan Ross: thanks. schedule-wise — maya when can we expect the quickstart email?
[22:19] Maya Chen: i'll send it after this call, within a couple hours. include credits and the sample notebook.
[22:55] Sam Ortiz: great. and liam when can we expect the benchmark sheet?
[22:59] Liam Patel: i'll send an initial draft by monday and we can iterate once we see your prompts.
[23:10] Priya Nair: monday works. thanks everyone.

[23:40] Maya Chen: thanks folks. recap of action items: maya send quickstart + credits; liam send benchmark + checklist; priya share prompts and traffic profile. we'll follow up with 2 proposed times for the SE demo. any final q's?
[24:02] Evan Ross: none from me. bye all.
[24:10] (Call ended)
